name: Purple with mosaic tail
description: White fuselage with the 'AIR CAIRO' wordmark across the forward windows, purple with an orange C and O. A purple fin with the stacked AIR CAIRO logo in white and orange; below it the whole rear fuselage, from the fin's root down past the aft door to the belly, is a mosaic of small triangles in purple, magenta, orange and yellow. 'aircairo.com' above the windows over the wing. Purple engines and winglets carrying the logo.

sources.title: Hannover Airport Air Cairo Airbus A320-251N SU-BUX (DSC00251) (CC BY-SA 4.0, MarcelX42)
sources.note: A320neo SU-BUX taxiing at Hannover, left side, close and level, 2024-09-05. Fitted to shapes/A20N.json (doors within 21 px: the aircraft is close, so perspective): the mosaic's forward edge traced, the wordmark's ends and height, the fin logo, aircairo.com.

sources.note: Right side from below on approach, 2024-08-11: the same layout from the right (wordmark forward, mosaic aft of the aft door, purple engines and fin).

sources.note: Left side from below, 2024-10-30: the wordmark repeated under the belly in purple and orange, the mosaic's lower edge.

mosaic.name: the tail mosaic's commonest colour (purple); its triangles are described in the logo

areas.name: the triangle mosaic over the rear fuselage, from the fin's root down past the aft door to the belly

titles.style: Heavy geometric capitals across the forward windows: the A's without crossbars and slanted, AIR in purple, then a big round orange C overlapping the next A, purple AIR and a round orange O.
Dark lower-case sans above the windows over the wing.

logos.description: The AIR CAIRO logo stacked in two lines: AIR in white over CAIRO with the C and O orange, the rest white, in the fin's middle.
The tail's mosaic: rows of small equilateral triangles (about 40 cm a side) in purple, magenta, orange and yellow, purple the commonest (about half), filling the area under it.
The stacked logo on the purple cowl.
Small Egyptian flag ahead of the registration, under the rear windows.

notes: Measured on SU-BUX (A320neo, left side, 2024-09-05) fitted to the A320neo shape; SU-BUK (right, 2024) and SU-BUM (left from below, 2024) agree. No Commons photo of SU-BVO (the maintainer's sighting) was found; same type, assumed the same scheme. The wordmark runs x 0.163-0.386, from the windows' bottoms to y 0.41, about 1.9 m tall. The mosaic's forward edge leaves the crown at x 0.747 (ahead of the fin's root) and curves down behind the aft door to the belly at x 0.83; it's drawn as one area in the mosaic's commonest colour, purple (about half its triangles; magenta, yellow, orange and dark red make up the rest, in triangles too small to draw as areas), and described as a logo. SU-BUX carried a '20 YEARS' badge under the cockpit in 2024 (the airline's anniversary), not drawn. The belly carries the wordmark again (SU-BUM); not drawn. Air Cairo's A320ceos may wear an older scheme.
